$comment: Declarative subagent roster AND capability curation. `model` is the canonical provider/model id a Task may be routed to — this file, not the TUI favorites list, is the source of truth for which models exist as subagents. Real costs/context come from models.dev via models-cache.json; price*/context here are offline fallbacks. lane: go-quota = OpenCode Go subscription; sub = user has a subscription (cheap regardless of list price); free = free tier; metered = pay-per-token.

profiles.name: OpenRouter GLM-5.3-Flash
profiles.avoid: All API-priced dispatch, including named requests
profiles.notes: Retained as catalog metadata only; never use for quota fallback.

profiles.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash / Vision Exp
profiles.best: fallback worker for vision-adjacent tasks when Muse unavailable; not default — Muse replaces it for standard coding
profiles.avoid: default dispatch — use Muse Spark 1.2 first; also novel architecture, when it loops, fail-closed types
profiles.notes: 284B/13B MoE; reasoning close to V4-Pro on simple agent tasks. No longer default — Muse is.

profiles.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
profiles.best: tiny utility/ops only when explicitly requesting cheapest 1M run — NOT default; prefer Muse even for ops/grunt/bulk/docs
profiles.avoid: default dispatch — Muse is default even for most ops; also complex multi-step debug, novel architecture
profiles.notes: Cheapest Go model with 1M ctx + structured output. 'Flash' is a name, not a speed guarantee. No longer default for ops — Muse is.

profiles.name: Hy3
profiles.avoid: everything. Never dispatch hy3, hy4-preview, or hy3-preview.
profiles.notes: Jon: never use Hy3 or Hy4 for anything. Review goes to Sol xhigh or GLM-5.3.

profiles.name: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (Free)
profiles.best: genuinely free (opencode zen, $0/$0) — same 90% of worker tasks as go-quota Muse: impl, tests, refactors, debugging, grunt, bulk edits, docs, parallel fan-out. Reach for it when go-quota Muse is capped, or to spare quota on low-stakes fan-out. Free is not a quality upgrade or an automatic override of a named model.
profiles.avoid: fail-closed types, security-sensitive work, anything needing guaranteed throughput — free lanes are usage-capped and can be rate-limited/deprioritized under load; when it takes shortcuts, escalate to Grok 4.6 (grok-sub) or Kimi, same as go-quota Muse. Do not treat as default over a named model.
profiles.notes: Must stay above the go-quota muse-spark profile in this array — matching is first-match substring (see model-router.ts inferProfile) and 'muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free' contains 'muse-spark-1.3-contributor', so ordering below it would misclassify this as go-quota lane. Distinct provider id (opencode/...) from go-quota opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor — same model family, different lane/limits. Confirmed against models-cache.json opencode/muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free row after the 2026-09-04 models.dev refresh: costInput 0, costOutput 0, context 1048576, output 131072 — matches the figures below exactly.

profiles.name: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor
profiles.best: DEFAULT WORKHORSE — 90% of worker tasks: impl, tests, refactors, debugging, UI/HUD, frontend, scene/codegen, grunt, bulk edits, docs, parallel fan-out, most coding
profiles.avoid: fail-closed types, security-sensitive, when it takes shortcuts → escalate to Grok 4.6 (grok-sub) or Kimi
profiles.notes: Go default as of 2026-09-02. 1.3 has no DeepSWE row yet; 1.2 xhigh was 55%. Same $0.10/$0.20 and 45k req/5h. Contributor trains on prompts. Fall back to 1.2 if 1.3 is blocked or dumb. Observed 1.2 shortcutting — escalate off Muse, not to Terra.

profiles.name: Kimi K3
profiles.best: design, creativity, novel architecture, long-horizon, huge context, multimodal, hard agentic
profiles.avoid: grunt, ops, utility runs, verifications - slow and quota-burning
profiles.notes: $3/$15 per 1M and slow - spend only on design/creative/architecture work.

profiles.name: GPT-6 Astra
profiles.best: PLAN-ONLY escalation per Jk (2026-09-04) — dispatch Astra only to plan against vague/open mandates (e.g. 'improve the quest system/MCP') where it can find the highest-leverage, rightest move no other model would; hand its plan to Muse (muse-spark-1.3-contributor, free or go-quota) to execute.
profiles.avoid: default dispatch, any execution/grunt/codegen/implementation work, tiny or well-specified tasks a cheaper model already handles — Astra is insanely smart and insanely expensive; burning it on execution defeats the point. Never a default ahead of Sol/Luna/Muse.
profiles.notes: Two explicit subscription transports with separate exact native pins. Never auto-select Astra. Plan-only: hand execution to Muse-free. Live discovery and dispatch verification determine availability; no silent provider substitution.

profiles.name: GPT-5.6 Luna Fast
profiles.best: approved sub-lane workhorse per Jk — cheap on the OpenAI sub ($0.2/$1.2), 1.05M ctx, reliable for general coding/impl/debugging/refactors; reach for it alongside or instead of go-quota Muse, not only as a last resort. Also when the user names it.
profiles.avoid: fail-closed types, security-sensitive work without review; still never a silent default ahead of a user-named model — routing is task x usage x speed x correctness, never a default
profiles.notes: OpenAI sub per Jk: effectively cheap and a good workhorse, not just an escalation. Sol remains the named/frontier escalation for hard design/architecture.

profiles.name: GPT-5.6 Luna Max
profiles.best: approved sub-lane workhorse per Jk — cheap on the OpenAI sub, 1M ctx, reliable general coding/impl/debugging; a good pick alongside go-quota Muse, not just a fallback. Pricier per-token than Luna Fast ($1/$6 vs $0.2/$1.2), so prefer Luna Fast when the cheaper tier is enough.
profiles.avoid: fail-closed types, security-sensitive work without review; still never a silent default ahead of a user-named model — routing is task x usage x speed x correctness, never a default
profiles.notes: Preferred future worker pin is provider=openai, model=gpt-5.6-luna, variant=max. Distinct from Luna Fast; the cursor-acp catalog's encoded gpt-5.6-luna-max is only a discoverable catalog representation. Sol remains the named/frontier escalation for hard design/architecture — Luna is the workhorse, Sol is the specialist.

profiles.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
profiles.best: when the user names it, or a cheaper model already failed - frontier reasoning, hard design, architecture

profiles.name: Grok 4.6
profiles.best: hard debugging, long rewrites, whole-file refactors, reasoning-heavy tasks when Muse takes shortcuts — fallback, not default (grok-sub only, never xai/*)
profiles.avoid: default dispatch, utility/ops, tiny edits — Muse is default; use Grok only for hard debugging/long rewrites/shortcut recovery
profiles.notes: Grok 4.6 rides the SuperGrok $30 plan via CLIProxyAPI 127.0.0.1:8317 (Grok Build OAuth). Do NOT use xai/grok-4.6. Do NOT use xai/grok-4.6 - that bills api.x.ai per token. 500k/500k context/output. Use only when Muse would shortcut or reasoning depth is needed — not default.

profiles.name: x-preview-f-free
profiles.avoid: production-critical or anything you need to trust
profiles.notes: Zen free preview; no quota cost.

profiles.name: Claude Code
profiles.best: when Jk picks Claude Code in the model picker, or Task(agent=claude-code) — official local CLI
profiles.avoid: auto-dispatch as a chat model; native Anthropic API assumptions; pinning a relay like x-preview/GLM/luna
profiles.notes: Not an API provider. openai-compatible bridge :3012 -> official `claude` CLI (`-p --output-format stream-json`). Auth is `claude auth login`. Picker identity claude-code/claude (also opus/sonnet).
